current.role: Middle (co-)author of 4 Atlas studies (SET2011, SET2012, SET2013, FER2026).
current.sub: Baylor College of Medicine · Houston, TX, USA
story: The Atlas lists 4 studies with Tuong Huynh as a middle author. SET2011 reports TFEB driving a coordinated autophagy and lysosome gene programme during starvation. SET2012 reports a signal from the lysosome to the nucleus in which mTOR-dependent phosphorylation of TFEB senses the state of the lysosome. SET2013 reports fasting switching on the TFEB gene in mouse liver, muscle and kidney, with TFEB driving its own transcription in a feed-forward loop that links starvation to lipid metabolism. FER2026 reports kidney-specific mouse models showing that mTORC1 hyperactivation, not TFEB/TFE3 activation alone, is the main driver of kidney cysts and tumours.

The three earlier papers list no affiliation for this author. A 2020 paper from the same group, with co-authors Settembre and Ballabio, lists Tuong Huynh at Baylor College of Medicine and Texas Children's Hospital in Houston, and the 2026 kidney paper gives Baylor as well.

studies.title: TFEB links autophagy to lysosomal biogenesis
studies.finding: Showed that TFEB drives a coordinated autophagy and lysosomal gene programme during starvation. In this paper TFEB was regulated by ERK2 phosphorylation; its control by mTORC1 at the lysosome was established in later work (SET2012).

studies.title: A lysosome-to-nucleus signalling mechanism senses and regulates the lysosome via mTOR and TFEB
studies.finding: A lysosome-to-nucleus mechanism uses mTOR-dependent TFEB phosphorylation to sense lysosomal state.

studies.title: TFEB controls cellular lipid metabolism through a starvation-induced autoregulatory loop
studies.finding: The authors found that fasting switches on the TFEB gene in mouse liver, muscle and kidney, and that TFEB drives its own transcription by binding CLEAR sites in its promoter, an autoregulatory loop that starvation strengthens. Liver TFEB overexpression changed 773 genes up and 611 down, with lipid catabolism as the top category, and acted largely through PGC-1alpha and PPARalpha: 74% of TFEB-induced genes failed to rise in mice lacking PPARalpha. Mice lacking liver TFEB built up liver fat and mobilised fat poorly during fasting and gained more weight on a high-fat diet, while liver TFEB overexpression prevented and halted diet-induced obesity and improved glucose tolerance in obese ob/ob mic

studies.title: Synergistic role of TFEB/TFE3 and mTORC1 in kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis
studies.finding: Using kidney-specific mouse models that genetically uncouple mTORC1 activity from TFEB/TFE3 activity (Depdc5-KO, RagC-KO, and Flcn/RagC double-KO), the authors show mTORC1 hyperactivation -- not TFEB/TFE3 activation alone -- is the primary driver of kidney cystogenesis and tumorigenesis in Birt-Hogg-Dube and Tuberous Sclerosis Complex models. Constitutive TFEB/TFE3 activity further accelerates disease on top of mTORC1-driven pathology.

story: Shiqi Lv was first author of a 2026 paper in Molecular Biomedicine (LV2026S) from Zhongshan Hospital in Shanghai. USP7 was raised in kidneys from people with chronic kidney disease. In two mouse models of kidney injury, USP7 kept the enzyme KDM5B from being degraded, which turned down TSC1 and let mTOR switch on and scar tissue form. Blocking USP7 genetically or with a drug reversed this in mice.

highlights.LV2026S: First author; PubMed lists the author in the Department of Nephrology at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University.

pubmed_affiliation: Department of Nephrology, Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, No. 180 Fenglin Road, Shanghai, 200032, China.

studies.title: Deubiquitinase USP7 stabilizes the histone demethylase KDM5B and promotes the progression of renal fibrosis through the TSC1/mTOR axis
studies.finding: USP7 deubiquitinates and stabilizes the histone demethylase KDM5B, which represses TSC1 transcription and thereby activates mTOR, promoting kidney fibrosis in two mouse injury models; USP7 is upregulated in human CKD kidneys and correlates with fibrosis severity. Genetic or pharmacological USP7 inhibition restores TSC1 expression, suppresses mTOR activation, and attenuates fibrosis in these mice, making the USP7-KDM5B-TSC1-mTOR axis a candidate intervention point; the human data are correlative only.

story: Hongxuan Feng was last author of a 2026 paper in Translational Stroke Research (MA2026), with 11 authors from the neurology department in Suzhou. In mice and cultured neurons, raising PIP4K2A reduced stroke-like brain injury. It lowered the TRIB3-p62 complex, improved autophagic flux and went with stronger AKT/mTOR signalling. The authors note that the small patient group in the study cannot show cause or tissue of origin.

story: The researchers used spatial transcriptomics and localized proteomics on human post-mortem brain tissue from people with Down syndrome and Alzheimer's disease changes. mTOR signalling was altered in particular parts of the hippocampus, and insulin signalling was altered in dentate granule neurons. The authors call the findings preliminary. Granholm is the last of fourteen authors, and PubMed lists the Department of Neurology at the University of Colorado Anschutz.

studies.title: Disruption of hippocampal upstream regulators of mTOR and insulin pathways in Down syndrome with Alzheimer's disease neuropathology: Preliminary observations
studies.finding: Spatial transcriptomics plus localized proteomics on human post-mortem hippocampus show that mTOR pathway signalling is significantly altered in specific hippocampal subfields in Down syndrome with Alzheimer's disease neuropathology, while insulin pathway signalling is altered specifically in dentate granule neurons — pointing to subregion- and cell-type-specific mTOR/insulin dysregulation rather than a uniform whole-tissue shift. Explicitly framed by the authors as preliminary.

story: Denisa Pirscoveanu was first author of a 2026 review article. It argues that treatments aimed at ageing pathways such as mTOR/TOR extend lifespan a lot in simple organisms like worms and flies, but much less in mammals. The authors point to many tissues sharing control, built-in redundancy and drug-handling complexity as reasons. As a review, it does not report new experiments. PubMed lists Pirscoveanu at the University of Medicine and Pharmacy Craiova.

highlights.PIR2026: First author of the review proposing that lifespan gains shrink in mammals because of system-level buffering.

pubmed_affiliation: Department of Neurology, University of Medicine and Pharmacy Craiova, Romania.

studies.title: Biological limits of lifespan extension: evidence for a shift from pathway leverage to system-level buffering across species
studies.finding: mTOR/TOR pathway interventions achieve large lifespan extensions in simple organisms but face declining efficacy in mammals due to distributed multi-tissue buffering, redundancy, and pharmacokinetic complexity - proposing a unifying framework for the translational challenge of aging pathway targeting.

story: Wei Huang is first author of an Atlas study (HUA2013) on memory. Mice lacking Rictor, a key part of mTORC2, in the forebrain had weaker long-term memory and weaker late-phase long-term potentiation, a lasting strengthening of connections between neurons. Flies lacking dTORC2 also had a long-term memory problem. Hippocampal actin polymerization was low in the mice, and restoring it fixed both defects. PubMed lists Huang at the Department of Neuroscience, Baylor College of Medicine.

highlights.HUA2013: First author: showed that deleting Rictor in mouse forebrain lowers mTORC2 activity, actin polymerization and long-term memory.

pubmed_affiliation: Department of Neuroscience, Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, Texas, USA.

studies.title: mTORC2 controls actin polymerization required for consolidation of long-term memory
studies.finding: Conditional deletion of Rictor in the postnatal mouse forebrain reduced mTORC2 activity and selectively impaired long-term memory and the late phase of hippocampal LTP, with a comparable long-term-memory deficit in dTORC2-deficient flies. Hippocampal actin polymerisation was reduced, and restoring it rescued both L-LTP and long-term memory; a compound that raised mTORC2 activity converted early LTP into late LTP and enhanced memory. story: Hiroshi Shimada was first author of a 2026 paper in the Atlas with Thomas Jansson and Fredrick J. Rosario among the senior authors. PubMed lists the author at the University of Colorado Anschutz and at Sapporo Medical University in Japan.

The team compared 46 placentas from uncomplicated term pregnancies. Male placentas showed stronger mTORC1 signalling, more System A amino acid transport and higher mitochondrial respiration than female ones. This is an observation at one time point, so it shows an association, not a cause.

highlights.SHIMADA2026: First author of the study comparing mTORC1 signalling and metabolism in male and female term placentas.

pubmed_affiliation: Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, University of Colorado Anschutz, Aurora, CO, USA

studies.title: Sexual Dimorphism in Placental mTORC1 Signaling, Amino Acid Transport, and Mitochondrial Respiration at Term.
studies.finding: In 46 term placentas, male placentas showed higher mTORC1 signalling (increased S6RP phosphorylation, reduced 4E-BP1), greater System A amino acid transport and higher mitochondrial respiratory capacity than female placentas, and male pregnancies had a higher birth-weight-to-placental-weight ratio. Observational: a cross-sectional association at a single timepoint, with no intervention and no randomisation, so the direction of the relationship between mTORC1 signalling and growth is not established here and residual confounding by maternal and obstetric factors cannot be excluded.

story: Lifu Zhu was first author of a 2026 mouse study on liver injury in animals sensitized to trichloroethylene, an industrial solvent. Loss of LKB1/AMPK signalling disturbed mTOR-controlled mitophagy, so damaged mitochondria leaked DNA into the cell and inflamed the liver. Rapamycin and AMPK activation protected the animals. There were no human data. PubMed lists Zhu at Anhui Medical University.

story: Kristen N Pollizzi was first author of a mouse study that separated the jobs of the two mTOR complexes in CD8 T cells. Cells with constantly active mTORC1 became strong, short-lived effector cells. Cells lacking mTORC1 kept memory features but responded poorly on a second exposure. mTORC2 activity influenced memory.

She is also a co-author of a mouse study showing that mTORC1 and mTORC2 steer helper T cells toward different fates. PubMed gives no affiliation in these records. A 2016 paper from the same group lists her at Johns Hopkins, and that is used here.

studies.title: mTORC1 and mTORC2 selectively regulate CD8+ T cell differentiation
studies.finding: By deleting Tsc2, Rheb or Rictor in T cells, this work split the CD8 response between the two mTOR complexes. Tsc2 loss left mTORC1 constitutively active: the cells were strongly glycolytic (high ECAR, high Slc2a1 and Pfk1, low spare respiratory capacity), made more IFN-gamma, TNF and granzyme B, cleared EL4 thymoma and slowed B16-OVA growth, but stayed terminally differentiated and were about two-fold fewer than wild type at day 30, with no memory. Rheb loss removed mTORC1 activity with mTORC2 intact: those cells failed as effectors but kept memory-like features and were about two-fold more numerous at day 30, yet did not respond to rechallenge, which the authors trace to metabolic defects.

studies.title: The kinase mTOR regulates the differentiation of helper T cells through the selective activation of signaling by mTORC1 and mTORC2
studies.finding: mTORC1 and mTORC2 selectively program distinct CD4 helper T-cell lineages.

story: Nan Zhou was first author of the Atlas study ZHOU2026 in the Journal of Molecular Histology. The enzyme TET1 removes methyl marks from the MRPS17 gene promoter, so MRPS17 is made in larger amounts in lung adenocarcinoma. More MRPS17 turns up PI3K-AKT-mTOR signalling and speeds up cell growth, migration and invasion. Knocking MRPS17 down caused cell death and slowed tumours in cells and mice. PubMed lists Zhou at Harbin Medical University.

highlights.ZHOU2026: First author: reported that TET1-driven MRPS17 expression activates PI3K-AKT-mTOR signalling in lung adenocarcinoma.

studies.title: TET1-mediated DNA demethylation and transcription activation of MRPS17 induces lung adenocarcinoma through PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway.
studies.finding: TET1 demethylates the MRPS17 promoter to drive MRPS17 overexpression in lung adenocarcinoma, activating PI3K-AKT-mTOR signalling and increasing proliferation, migration and invasion. MRPS17 knockdown induces apoptosis and suppresses tumour growth in vitro and in vivo.

story: Jingting Xu was first author of the Atlas study XU2026B in Inflammation Research. It is a review of what mTORC2, built around the RICTOR protein, does in immune cells. It covers T cell, B cell, macrophage, dendritic cell and NK cell roles. In tissue inflammation its effects depend on the setting: it worsens osteoarthritis and pancreatitis but dampens pro-inflammatory polarization in colorectal cancer. PubMed lists Xu at Tongji Hospital in Wuhan.

highlights.XU2026B: First author: wrote the review on mTORC2/RICTOR in immune cells and inflammatory diseases.

pubmed_affiliation: Department of Orthopedics, Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, 430030, Hubei, China.

studies.title: The role of mTORC2/RICTOR in immune cells and inflammatory diseases.
studies.finding: mTORC2/RICTOR signaling (via AKT, SGK1, PKC) shapes Th1/Th2 differentiation, Treg stability, memory T cell formation, BCR signaling and plasma cell survival, and macrophage/DC/NK function; its role in tissue inflammation is context-dependent (exacerbating osteoarthritis and pancreatitis but restraining pro-inflammatory polarization in colorectal cancer), and dual mTORC1/2 inhibitors (e.g. AZD2014) show early but complicated promise.

studies.finding: Corilagin restores chondrocyte autophagic flux and ECM synthesis by inhibiting PI3K/AKT/mTOR and NF-κB signalling, reducing cartilage erosion and OARSI scores in the mouse DMM osteoarthritis model.

current.lab_name: Department of Orthopedics, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology (Wuhan, Hubei, China)
current.role: First author of a 2026 study linking impaired chaperone-mediated autophagy to mTORC1 activation in intervertebral disc degeneration.
current.sub: Department of Orthopedics, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
story: Xianglong Chen was first author of a 2026 paper in Advanced Science. PubMed lists the author in the Department of Orthopedics at Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology in Wuhan.

The study looked at degeneration of the discs between the vertebrae. In disc cells from patients and in rat models, a clean-up pathway called chaperone-mediated autophagy was weakened. A protein called midnolin then built up, destroyed TSC2 and switched mTORC1 on, which drove cell senescence and tissue breakdown. Blocking midnolin, restoring the pathway or giving rapamycin reduced the damage in cells and rats.

highlights.CHEN2026C: First author of the study tracing disc degeneration to midnolin-driven loss of TSC2 and mTORC1 activation.

pubmed_affiliation: Department of Orthopedics, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, Wuhan, China.

studies.title: Impaired Chaperone-Mediated Autophagy Accelerates Intervertebral Disc Degeneration by Inducing MIDN Accumulation to Target TSC2 for Proteasomal Degradation
studies.finding: Loss of chaperone-mediated autophagy lets its substrate midnolin (MIDN) accumulate; MIDN binds TSC2 and drives its proteasomal degradation independently of ubiquitination, de-repressing mTORC1 and causing senescence, SASP and matrix loss in disc cells. MIDN knockdown, LAMP2A overexpression or rapamycin each blocked the degeneration - a new upstream route to mTORC1 hyperactivation.

current.role: First author of a 2026 mouse study of the mTOR inhibitor everolimus in head and neck cancer.
current.sub: Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery · Louisiana State University Health, Shreveport, USA
story: In mouse models of TP53-mutant head and neck cancer, a tumour type that often escapes the immune system, the mTOR inhibitor everolimus slowed tumour growth. It brought more killer T cells and dendritic cells into the tumour, reduced regulatory T cells, and lowered PD-1 and PD-L1 levels, which restored T-cell activity. Nath is the first of nine authors, and PubMed lists the otolaryngology department at LSU Health Shreveport.

highlights.NAT2026: First of nine authors on the mouse study of everolimus reshaping the immune environment of TP53-mutant head and neck tumours.

pubmed_affiliation: Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, Louisiana State University Health, Shreveport, LA, 71103, USA.

studies.title: mTOR inhibition augments antitumor immune effector response by reprogramming the TP53-mutant, immune-cold HNSCC tumor microenvironment
studies.finding: In syngeneic TP53-mutant HNSCC mouse models, the mTOR inhibitor everolimus reprogrammed the immune-cold tumor microenvironment: it increased CD8+ T cell and dendritic cell infiltration, reduced Tregs and HIF-1α/VEGFA-driven MDSC recruitment, boosted TNF-α/CXCL10 chemokine signaling, and reduced PD-1/PD-L1 expression — restoring T-cell cytotoxic competence and suppressing tumor growth.

story: Yang Zong was last author of a 2026 pathology study that looked for a better test to spot certain kidney tumors. These tumors carry changes in the FLCN, TSC or MTOR genes or in TFE transcription factors. The team found that the protein GPR143 shows up in staining of these tumors and can work alongside the existing marker GPNMB. This was a tissue and database study, not a treatment trial. PubMed lists Zong at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

highlights.LI2026: Last author of the study proposing GPR143 staining as a diagnostic marker for kidney tumors with FLCN/TSC/MTOR-TFE alterations.

studies.title: GPR143, a novel immunohistochemical marker for renal tumors with FLCN/TSC/MTOR-TFE alterations.
studies.finding: GPR143 is a sensitive and specific immunohistochemical biomarker for renal tumors driven by FLCN/TSC/MTOR-TFE pathway alterations, offering a practical diagnostic tool beyond existing ancillary tests.

story: N Valerio Dorrello is first author of a 2006 paper in Science. In cultured cells, the kinase S6K1 phosphorylates the tumor suppressor PDCD4, and the ubiquitin ligase betaTRCP then marks it for destruction. Losing PDCD4 lets translation and cell growth go ahead. PubMed lists him at the Department of Pathology, NYU Cancer Institute, New York University School of Medicine.

highlights.DOR2006: First author of the study showing that S6K1 and betaTRCP degrade PDCD4 to promote translation.

studies.finding: S6K1 triggers betaTRCP-mediated degradation of the tumour suppressor PDCD4 to promote translation.

story: Simon C. Johnson is first author of an Atlas review (JOH2013), meaning it summarizes earlier work and has no new experiments. It argues that blocking the mTOR pathway lengthens life in several species and protects against a growing list of age-related diseases. It also notes that side effects of current mTOR inhibitors make them unsuitable for healthy people. PubMed lists Johnson at the Department of Pathology, University of Washington.

highlights.JOH2013: First author: wrote the Nature review that summarizes mTOR's role in ageing and age-related disease.

pubmed_affiliation: Department of Pathology, University of Washington, Seattle, Washington 98195, USA.

studies.title: mTOR is a key modulator of ageing and age-related disease
studies.finding: The landmark Nature review that put mTOR at the center of aging biology. Lays out the case that inhibiting mTOR extends lifespan across species and guards against a growing list of age-related diseases - while being candid that side effects currently block its use in healthy people. Excellent orientation map for the whole field.
